title: Google AI Studio uses Gemini to build Android apps with sign-in and storage, ready to install on your phone
summary: If you wanted an Android app with sign-in, data persistence, and AI features, you used to have to set up a backend, manage API keys, and plug in a cable to sideload the build. Now you describe what you need in Google AI Studio, leave the rest to the Build agent, and install the result straight onto your phone.
ai_summary: The Build agent in Google AI Studio can now generate complete Android apps with Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen: you describe the idea, it provisions a Cloud Firestore database and Google Sign-In, keeps Gemini API credentials server-side, then publishes the app to your personal Google Play library so you can install it on your phone. The updated emulator supports 1200p high-definition streaming, real-time audio, and screenshot feedback for UI changes. Google says you can publish in minutes, and building and testing on Play is free. It's aimed at people who want to prototype quickly and validate on a real device; so far the story is entirely within Google's Firebase and Play ecosystem, and the original post doesn't spell out pricing or a timeline.
brief: The Build agent automatically provisions Cloud Firestore, Google Sign-In, and Firebase AI Logic, so Gemini API keys no longer get packaged inside the APK.
The emulator gets an upgrade: 1200p HD streaming, real-time audio, and a toolbar button that sends screenshots back to the agent for UI changes.
You can publish straight to your personal Google Play library; Google says it takes minutes, and building and testing are free.
Under the hood, it now uses the official Android CLI to scaffold projects, look up documentation, and run Gradle builds.

sections.h: What this is: a Build agent that creates full-stack Android apps

blocks.p: Google AI Studio is Google's web workspace for developers to chat with Gemini, generate code, and debug it. Inside it, the Build agent is a multi-step agent that breaks down tasks and executes them one step at a time.

This update moves it from generating code snippets to producing complete, store-ready Android apps: with Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen, you describe an app idea and it automatically configures data storage, user sign-in, and AI features, generates production-grade Kotlin code, and publishes the result to your personal Google Play library.

callout.title: This isn't just about drawing screens.
callout.text: It also handles backend configuration, credential security, and signing for release, and generates Kotlin code with both a data layer and an AI layer.

sections.h: From idea to phone: the steps the agent handles for you

blocks.p: Before, Android apps generated by AI Studio could only store data in a local session that disappeared when the app closed. Now the Build agent reads your prompt first and decides whether the app needs persistent data, user sign-in, or generative AI capabilities.

After you confirm, it automatically handles these steps: creates a Cloud Firestore database and writes security rules; sets up Google Sign-In; keeps Gemini API credentials server-side; and generates clean, idiomatic Kotlin code.

sections.h: The old detours are now gone

blocks.p: Installing your own app on a phone used to be more annoying than expected: either enable USB debugging and connect a cable, manage a signing keystore locally, or set up a full developer console account.

Now Google Play is integrated directly into Google AI Studio: set up a Play account in a few clicks from the publish panel, and AI Studio builds and signs the Android App Bundle (.aab) behind the scenes. You then download and install it on your phone straight from Play. Google says the whole process takes minutes, and building and testing on Play is free.

sections.h: Data, sign-in, and credentials: how the backend is wired automatically

blocks.p: Cross-device sync: the agent provisions a Cloud Firestore database, configures the Firebase Android SDKs, and generates security rules tailored to your data model. Users can start a session on a tablet and continue on their phone; offline changes are cached and sync automatically when the connection returns.

Sign-in: when the app needs user profiles or private workspaces, the agent configures Firebase Authentication with Google Sign-In and adds per-user authorization rules so each person can read and write only their own documents.

Credential security: hardcoding an API key in a client APK risks it being extracted. The agent now automatically configures Firebase AI Logic and enforces Firebase App Check, which is backed by Google Fraud Defense (formerly reCAPTCHA Enterprise). Credentials stay server-side, and App Check verifies that requests come from your genuine, untampered app—both in the browser emulator and on Play.

sections.h: What actually makes the emulator better?

blocks.p: Mobile UI work depends heavily on a see-and-try feedback loop, and this release changes several parts of the emulator and debugging flow. Startup latency is noticeably lower, and an HD toggle in the toolbar switches the stream to 1200p, making it easier to check Jetpack Compose spacing, animations, and dense layouts.

Sound is now available too: the emulator's audio plays in real time in the browser, so you can test Gemini Live API voice companions, text-to-speech (TTS) coaches, sound-enabled games, and media apps without leaving Google AI Studio.

UI changes no longer require long text descriptions: Take a screenshot in the toolbar captures the current screen and attaches it to your prompt, so Gemini can edit the Kotlin UI with the image as context—for example, tightening card padding, fixing contrast, or realigning the toolbar.

sections.h: What kinds of apps can you build?

blocks.p: Google provides several prompts you can try directly and lists a few kinds of apps well-suited to the new capabilities.

items.desc: Uses the Gemini API to generate personalized daily workouts, reads cues aloud, and saves history across devices with Firestore and Google Sign-In.

items.desc: Users sign in with Google, snap photos of ingredients to generate recipe ideas, sync shared grocery lists in Firestore, and use custom serif typography.

list: Pricing: the post only says building and testing on Play is free. It doesn't explain billing for Firestore, Authentication, or AI Logic beyond free tiers, nor the per-call price of Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen.
Rollout timeline: it says 'launching today,' but doesn't say when it reaches each region or account cohort.
Sign-in options: only Google Sign-In is mentioned; there's no word on email/password, phone number, or third-party login support.
Quantified gains: the emulator's 'lower latency' has no specific number and no quantitative comparison with the old version.
Generation limits: it doesn't say at what project size, screen count, or business-logic complexity the generated code starts needing manual fixes.

blocks.p: The biggest value is removing the most tedious engineering work—backend, security, and signing for release—so ideas reach a real device faster. The trade-off is deep lock-in to Google's ecosystem: data in Firebase, distribution through Play, and models from Gemini.

list: If you often build quick prototypes, demos, or personal tools and want to skip database setup and signing, it's worth starting an Android project to try.
If you already have a mature backend or aren't in Google's ecosystem, treat it as a fast generator for Kotlin code and UI, then wire in your own services.
If you plan a production release, check that the Firestore security rules and App Check configuration meet your data compliance requirements.
